tasks.title: PersonaResolver: casefolded tier lookup + same-tier collision detection + casefolded cache key
tasks.notes: In __init__: casefold Tier-1 (settings.persona_role_map) and Tier-2 (self._tier2_map) keys; if two distinct original keys in the SAME tier casefold identically, raise PersonaResolutionError(role=<casefolded key>, reason="ambiguous_case_collision") at construction (uncaught, propagates through create_app() like a malformed Tier-2 YAML already does). _resolve_uncached's Tier-3 WHERE clause casefolds the incoming role and raises the same error at resolve time if the query returns >1 distinct persona for it. Cache key becomes casefold(role) throughout resolve()/the cache dict. Regression test: reproduce today's exact-case mappings (cio:cio, architect:architect, developer:developer, product-manager:product-manager, engineering-manager:engineering-manager) and assert each still resolves identically post-change (AC-21).

tasks.title: PersonaResolver: 3-tier persona precedence config loading
tasks.notes: Tier-1: settings.persona_precedence_order (parsed at Settings load, T-01). Tier-2: new precedence: root key in persona_role_map.yaml, loaded at __init__ alongside self._tier2_map — malformed value (not a list of strings) is a startup error, uncaught. Tier-3: SELECT rank, persona FROM persona_precedence ORDER BY rank via the same injectable session_factory + 3.0s asyncio.wait_for timeout as _resolve_tier3; cache the resolved order in-process for 300s under a reserved sentinel cache key distinct from any role string (DATA-DESIGN.md §6). All three empty/unset -> hardcoded default ["cio","architect","product-manager","engineering-manager","developer"]. Add services/api/config/persona_role_map.yaml's precedence: key (or leave absent to exercise the default) as part of this task's test fixtures, not the shipped file's runtime default.

tasks.title: PersonaResolver: multi-role precedence selection + persona_mapping_not_found event
tasks.notes: Add resolve_precedence(roles: list[str]) -> str (D-06): refactor _resolve_uncached's per-tier fallthrough into a shared, NON-raising helper returning persona|None so this method can try every surviving role without triggering a false-positive persona_mapping_not_found per losing candidate. Collect (role, persona) candidates in original token order; winner = first persona in precedence order (T-04) present among candidates; return casefold(winning role) (never the persona). If candidates is empty, emit logger.info("persona_mapping_not_found", extra={roles: <full survivor list>, tiers_consulted: ["tier-1-env","tier-2-yaml","tier-3-postgres"], timestamp}) then raise PersonaNotFoundError. Also add the SAME event emission to the EXISTING single-role _resolve_uncached's own all-3-tier-miss branch (roles=[role]) so AUTH-07-TC-02's direct resolve("nonexistent-role") call (and every existing rbac-checks consumer) also gets it — resolve()'s public signature/behavior is otherwise unchanged. Use the _RecordCapturingHandler pattern (attached directly to app.core.persona_resolver's logger, force-enabled, de-propagated) for every log assertion — Alembic's fileConfig(disable_existing_loggers=True) makes caplog/capsys pass vacuously after any migrated_db test (C-4). NFR-performance test: extend FakeSessionFactory-based test asserting call_count stays 0 for the ['Architect','Developer','developer'] regression case (all three resolve via Tier-2, confirming no new Tier-3 I/O is introduced by ranking).

tasks.title: GET /auth/logout route + dashboard_logout event
tasks.notes: _LOGOUT_PATH (D-01) added alongside _AUTHORIZE_PATH/_TOKEN_PATH. New route folds frontend_login_url into the SAME config_completeness_gate style check _require_oidc_configured already uses for the OIDC triple (unset frontend_login_url OR incomplete OIDC triple -> 501, same envelope). 302 to f"{issuer}{_LOGOUT_PATH}?{urlencode({'client_id': client_id, 'post_logout_redirect_uri': frontend_login_url})}" — never id_token_hint. Reads the optional incoming Authorization bearer header (D-08) and decodes it via the SAME _peek_kid + jwks_cache.get_signing_key + jwt.decode().validate() path _log_dashboard_login already uses, falling back to user_id="unknown" on any decode failure or missing header — never blocks the redirect. Emits logger.info("dashboard_logout", extra={user_id}) on every completed redirect (the 501 path does NOT emit — only a completed, config-satisfied end-session redirect logs, mirroring dashboard_login's success-only convention). AC-13's actual SSO-termination behavior is manual-verification-only (no local Keycloak) — this task's tests cover URL construction, the 501 gate, and the log event only.

tasks.title: Frontend GET /logout Route Handler
tasks.notes: Order (D-08): readSession() first (to capture the pre-clear accessToken) -> clearSession() -> fetch(`${getApiBaseUrl()}/auth/logout`, {headers: session ? {Authorization: `Bearer ${session.accessToken}`} : {}, redirect: "manual", signal: AbortSignal.timeout(5000)}) -> relay the 302's Location header via NextResponse.redirect, mirroring login/route.ts's uniform generic-502-on-any-failure handling (missing Location, non-3xx, thrown/timed-out fetch). No new UI anywhere (AC-15) — this file is the ENTIRE deliverable, no mockup/component touched. AC-14 is structural (dashboard_session is path:"/", single session for every route, already true) — test asserts this handler calls clearSession() unconditionally even when no prior session exists (idempotent) and never short-circuits the relay.
